In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence that carotid endarterectomy (CEA) is superior to carotid stent placement (CSP) for the treatment of symptomatic carotid artery stenosis.
the use of carotid artery stents in patients with carotid artery disease is not associated with a significant increased risk of ischemic stroke or death at 30 days or 1 year.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
carotid stent placement can cause a transient, benign, leptomeningeal contrast enhancement on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
the carotid bifurcation is a site where the carotid artery is most likely to become occluded.

carotid stents are associated with a low incidence of leptomeningeal contrast enhancement on follow-up magnetic resonance images (MRIs), which is not associated with clinical or radiographic evidence of intracranial atherosclerosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
leptomeningeal (arachnoid) enhancement on MRI is a common finding after carotid artery stenting and is not necessarily indicative of a new or enlarging aneurysm.
carotid stenosis is not a benign condition, and that carotid endarterectomy (CEA) and carotid stent placement (CSP) can be associated with stroke.
carotid artery stenting is safe and effective.
